Just hours after announcing Apple's support for communities affected by wildfires in Southern Europe, Tim Cook said the company is also donating to aid relief efforts following the earthquake in Kumamoto, Japan. Details below.

Apple to donate to Japan's relief efforts

Apple CEO Tim Cook once again took to X to announce Apple's plans to assist communities affected by natural disasters.

Cook said the company is donating to support Japan's relief efforts, adding that the country "holds a very special place in (his) heart." You can see his full post below:

On Tuesday afternoon, a magnitude 7.1 earthquake struck Kumamoto Prefecture in southern Japan, with the epicenter located about 12 miles south of Kumamoto City. It has so far claimed 34 lives, left thousands homeless, and tens of thousands of households remain without water or electricity.

According to Reuters, ongoing aftershocks and extreme heat in the region have further hampered rescue and recovery efforts.

Cook's announcement comes just hours after he said Apple would help millions of people affected by wildfires in Southern Europe, continuing Apple's tradition of lending a hand during natural disasters and other emergencies.

Apple also has an internal donation program called "Employee Giving," which has raised more than US$880 million to date through its donation matching policy.
